title: What If the Sahara Stopped Feeding the Amazon?

scenes.text: What if the Sahara stopped feeding the Amazon? The world's biggest rainforest quietly depends on a desert.
Every year, about twenty-seven million tons of Saharan dust settle over the Amazon basin.
It comes mostly from an ancient dry lake bed in Chad, and it rides the trade winds across the Atlantic.
Only a tiny share is phosphorus, about twenty-two thousand tons a year. But rainforest soil is starved of it.
Heavy rain and floods wash away roughly that same amount every year. The dust refills what the rain removes.
Cut the dust off, and the Amazon's phosphorus supply would shrink every year. The biggest forest on Earth is fed by a desert.
